title: Triage tests pass on a host with no git identity; a read-only triage listing needs no actor
description: epic/2jn CI fails deterministically on TestTriageJSONListsTheUntriagedForAnAgent (triage_test.go:86) and TestTheEpicPrefixIsAcceptedEverywhere (:386): 'ticfac triage qeu: --by names who is triaging, and this checkout's git config names nobody'. The CI runner has no git identity; this Mac does, so it passes locally (reproduce with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1). Cause: internal/cli/triage.go:225 calls triageActor for every invocation, including the read-only --json listing. Fix both: (1) a listing (--json with no settling action) does not resolve an actor at all — only an action that records a decision needs --by or a git identity (decided 2026-09-27: a read needs no author); (2) newFindingsRepo (findings_test.go:27) isolates the test from host git config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=os.DevNull) and sets user.name in the fixture checkout, as triage_test.go:317-319 already does.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'Triage|EpicPrefix' passes with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1; a test asserts ticfac triage <epic> --json succeeds with no identity and a settling action without one is still refused
